# Project Deep-Dive + ML Fundamentals Discussion

[← Waymo](../README.md) · [Every Waymo question](../../waymo.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/project-deep-dive-ml-fundamentals)

`deep-dive` `ml-knowledge` `open-ended` `presentation`

---

## Expectations

- Explain 1–3 previous projects in detail, usually those included on your resume.
- The interviewer controls the discussion, so anticipate interruptions every 1–3 minutes for clarifications or probing challenges.
- ML fundamentals are layered into the conversation: derivations, loss-function choices, evaluation measures, debugging methods, and alternatives you considered but declined.
- In senior loops (L5+), prepare to cover the organizational setting — who made decisions, which tradeoffs were discarded, and what you would change in hindsight.

## Expectations (continued)

There is no formal slide presentation because the round is conversational. A whiteboard or shared document is generally available for drawing or notes.

## Notes

- **Choose projects that have depth.** A single thoroughly understood project is better than three superficial ones. The interviewer may spend 20+ minutes on one project, so select work that lets you withstand five layers of “why did you select X instead of Y?” questioning.
- **Attach numbers to every claim.** Include data volume (rows, GB, tokens), model scale (parameters, FLOPS), training expense ($, GPU-hours), and ablation changes (point improvements or regressions). General statements will be examined aggressively.
- **Ablations provide the clearest evidence.** A well-organized ablation table shows that you personally conducted the experiment instead of merely learning about its outcome. Commit 2–3 ablation results per project to memory.
- **Failure modes.** Clearly acknowledge what failed and the reason it failed. The strongest narrative form is, “We tested X, it performed poorly because Y, and we therefore moved to Z.”
- **Separate your contribution from the team’s.** Senior interviewers pay close attention to scope. Say, “I handled X, the team owned Y, and we decided Z together”; presenting team efforts as your own is a repeated warning sign.
- **ML fundamentals to review before the round (the selection depends on your resume topics):**
  - Loss-function derivations: cross-entropy with softmax, MSE, focal loss, and contrastive losses.
  - Optimizer behavior: SGD with momentum versus Adam, weight decay, and warmup schedules.
  - Regularization methods: dropout, weight decay, augmentation, and early stopping.
  - Evaluation: precision, recall, F1, calibration (ECE and reliability diagrams), and distributional measures (KS and Wasserstein).
  - Typical bug patterns: data leakage, noisy labels, train-test contamination, confounded ablations, and shifts in the evaluation distribution.
- **Common round dynamics reported in this loop.** The interviewer may courteously steer you back — “that’s an interesting tangent; let me return you to X” — so manage your time accordingly. One reported failure pattern is repeated redirection by the interviewer while the candidate fails to adjust their pace.

## Preparation

- Create a one-page outline for each project covering the problem, data, approach, major decisions, ablations, results, and lessons. Practice without prompts until you can reach any bullet within 30 seconds.
- Rehearse with a peer who interrupts forcefully, and practice changing context without dropping the main thread.
- Review the ML fundamentals list above one week before the loop. Skim and re-derive on paper anything that does not return immediately.
- Prepare 2–3 reflections for each project on what you would do differently. These are the questions L5+ interviewers prioritize most.
